reference_title: Drilled Shafts: Construction Procedures and LRFD Design Methods

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Lateral loading typically controls the diameter of drilled shafts for highway bridges and may also control embedded length for retaining walls, noise walls, and sign/light standard foundations. Both geotechnical and structural design are required; structural design covered in Chapter 12. For rigorous coverage of laterally loaded deep foundations see FHWA GEC 9 (Parkes et al., 2018). This chapter does not explicitly address seismic design, but the methods can be used to determine linear or nonlinear spring constants for bases of structural columns for dynamic analysis.
key_points: Lateral loading typically controls shaft diameter; may control embedded length for retaining walls/sign structures
For detailed treatment see FHWA GEC 9 (Parkes et al., 2018)
Methods provide spring constants for structural dynamic analysis
sections.applicability: All drilled shafts subject to lateral loading; bridge piers, retaining walls, sign structures

sections.title: Examples of Lateral Loading Applications
sections.body: Sources of lateral loads: earth pressures, centrifugal forces, braking, wind, current/wave forces, ice loads, vessel impact, and earthquakes. Monoshaft (single drilled shaft supporting single column): small footprint advantage; growing use for aesthetics. Caltrans Type I: continuous cage from shaft to column. Caltrans Type II: shaft ≥18 in. larger diameter — designed to force plastic hinge at column base during seismic event rather than at depth. Groups of shafts: cap provides rotational restraint and transfers column bending moments to axial forces in shafts; better for large lateral loads from vessel impact, seismic, ice, or wind. Bridge over water: foundation must accommodate wind, current/waves, vessel impact, seismic, ice, centrifugal forces, braking plus scour. Sound walls, sign structures, high mast lighting: dominated by wind overturning; single-shaft resists moment and shear in bending; two-shaft resists moment as push-pull couple plus some bending for shear. Abutments: resist lateral forces from earth pressure, traffic surcharge, braking, thermal, seismic. Retaining structures: secant and tangent pile walls; may be tied back with anchors if cantilever is insufficient. Slope stabilization: shaft wall across slip surface increases resisting forces in soil.
key_points: Caltrans Type I: continuous cage shaft-to-column; Type II: shaft ≥18 in. larger to force plastic hinge at column base in seismic event
Groups with cap: rotational restraint; moment transferred as axial forces in shafts
Sound wall/sign/lighting: wind controls; two-shaft = push-pull couple for moment + bending for shear
Slope stabilization: shaft wall across slip surface increases soil resistance

sections.title: Design for Lateral Loading
sections.body: Three design conditions: (1) Geotechnical Strength Limit State — sufficient size and depth to support factored loads without collapse; critical for transient wind or extreme event (vessel impact, seismic); (2) Structural Strength Limit State — sufficient size and reinforcement to resist moment, shear, and axial demands; (3) Service Limit State — deformations and rotations within tolerable limits; requires determination of foundation stiffness for structural analysis. Design is Block 10 in the overall process of Chapter 8. Design subsurface profile must consider scour and liquefaction; different profiles may be needed for different load cases.
key_points: Three limit states: geotechnical strength, structural strength, service (deformation control)
Design is Block 10 of overall process (Figure 8-1 in Chapter 8)
Scour and liquefaction may require different subsurface profiles for different load cases

sections.title: Planning Stage Estimates
sections.body: Broms' method: simple closed-form solution for planning stage estimates. Short rigid pile in cohesive soil: passive pressure p = 9su from depth 1.5B; fails by rotation; Hu = 9suBL(0.5L - e); Mu = 0.5HuL (simplifications). Short rigid pile in cohesionless soil: Hu = 3BKpγH²/2. Long flexible pile (structural failure): moment demand used to design reinforcement. Broms method does NOT provide lateral deformations — use p-y method for service limit state. Log spiral method: rational approach for short rigid piles in rock.
key_points: Broms method: planning stage only; does NOT compute deformations
Use p-y method for service limit state (deformation) evaluation
Short pile in clay: passive = 9su below 1.5B; Short pile in sand: Kp passive
Long flexible pile: structural failure mode — design for maximum moment
sections.applicability: Planning stage lateral load estimates; preliminary design

sections.title: Computational Procedures and Design Methodology (p-y Method)
sections.body: P-y curve method is the standard analytical tool. Soil/rock modeled as nonlinear Winkler springs: p = lateral soil resistance per unit length (kN/m); y = lateral deflection (m). Shaft modeled as elastic beam-column. Provides shear, moment, and deflection vs. depth. Standard p-y curve formulations: (1) Soft clay below GWT (Matlock 1970): p/pu = 0.5(y/y50)^(1/3) for y ≤ 8y50; p = 0.72pu for y > 8y50 (static); p = 0.72pu plateau (cyclic); pu = min(3suB + σ'vB + JsuZ, 9suB); y50 = 2.5ε50B; (2) Stiff clay below GWT (Reese et al. 1975): different formulation for static vs. cyclic loading; (3) Sand (Reese et al. 1974 / O'Neill-Murchison 1983): A*pu/kz for small y; pu = min(C1H + C2B)γ'H, C3γ'HB) effective stress-based; k (initial modulus of subgrade reaction) tabulated vs. friction angle; (4) Weak rock (Reese 1997): p-y based on uniaxial compressive strength; (5) Strong rock (Carter & Kulhawy 1992): p-y based on mass shear modulus. Boundary conditions: free head (M=0, no rotation restraint at top — typical for monoshaft); fixed head (rotation=0 — pile cap); partial fixity via rotational spring. Computer programs: COM624P, LPILE, FB-Multipier, OpenSees, FB-Deep, SHAFT. Key outputs: maximum moment and its depth; shear force profile; lateral deflection at shaft top; rotation at shaft top.
key_points: P-y method: soil = nonlinear Winkler springs; shaft = elastic beam-column
Soft clay (Matlock 1970): p/pu = 0.5(y/y50)^(1/3); pu = min(9suB, 3suB + σ'vB + JsuZ); y50 = 2.5ε50B
Sand p-y: k (initial modulus) tabulated vs. friction angle; effective stress-based pu
Boundary conditions: free head (M=0 at top) or fixed head (rotation=0) or rotational spring
Computer programs: COM624P, LPILE, FB-Multipier, OpenSees
equations: Soft clay (Matlock 1970): p/pu = 0.5(y/y50)^(1/3) for y ≤ 8y50; p = 0.72pu for y > 8y50
pu = min(9suB, 3suB + σ'vB + JsuZ) — ultimate lateral resistance per unit length of shaft
y50 = 2.5ε50B — reference deflection at 50% ultimate resistance
sections.applicability: Final design lateral analysis; AASHTO strength and service limit state checks

sections.title: Design for Seismic Loading
sections.body: Seismic is Extreme Event I limit state per AASHTO. Two types of loading: (1) kinematic interaction — free-field ground motions impose deformations on foundation; (2) inertial interaction — structural mass vibrates and imposes forces on foundation. Liquefaction effects: evaluate liquefaction potential; post-liquefaction residual strength; p-y curves for liquefied soil use reduced resistance; lateral spreading imposes passive forces on shaft above liquefied zone; shaft tip must extend into non-liquefiable bearing stratum. Cyclic softening of cohesive soils: modified p-y curves; cyclically softened shear strength for sensitive clays. Foundation stiffness for structural analysis: secant stiffness (force/deflection) and rotational stiffness; typically represented as 3×3 or 6×6 stiffness matrix or equivalent depth of fixity. Caltrans Type II: force plastic hinge at column base, not in shaft at depth where inspection/repair is difficult.
key_points: Seismic: Extreme Event I limit state per AASHTO
Kinematic + inertial interaction both contribute to seismic loading
Liquefied soil: reduced p-y resistance; extend shaft below liquefiable zone
Lateral spreading: passive forces on shaft above liquefied zone
Foundation stiffness matrix or depth of fixity for structural dynamic analysis
sections.applicability: Seismic design in Zones 2, 3, and 4; liquefaction-affected sites; high seismic regions

sections.title: Summary
sections.body: Chapter provided guidance on design of drilled shafts for lateral loading including applications, design process, planning stage estimates, detailed analysis using p-y curves, and seismic considerations. P-y method is the standard analytical tool. Structural design of reinforced concrete per Chapter 12. See FHWA GEC 9 for comprehensive treatment.
